parole.testo: A learned αντιδάνειο (antidáneio, “repatriated loanword”). Learned borrowing from Italian arcipelago, from Byzantine Greek Ἀρχιπέλαγος (Arkhipélagos) which is Ancient Greek ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “main”) + πέλαγος (pélagos, “sea”), a designation for the Aegean Sea. Attested since 1728 in Katharevousa as ἀρχ

parole.significato: scope, telescope, spyglass, field glass; a portable optical instrument containing a lens used for magnification to see…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian occhiali (“eyeglasses”), the apheresis perhaps resulting via crasis of article το (to) with an earlier Byzantine Greek ὀκκιάλιν (okkiálin).
From Italian pappagallo, from Byzantine Greek παπαγᾶς (papagâs), from Arabic بَبَّغَاء (babbaḡāʔ), of onomatopoeic origin.
